title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page has two parts.

**End of the previous discussion (top of the page).** On the previous page Grothendieck introduced a 'Legendre épi-structure' subordinate to a section α of μ_4^* ∧ ω_J, and the μ_2-torsor of such structures. He proved (57): Isom_{S,J}(E_α, E) ≅ L_α(E). This makes E_α universal among elliptic curves of 'type (J, t)'.

Here he notes a variant. Suppose one has a section ω of ω_J itself (a trivialisation of the line ω_J). Then one gets a canonical curve E_ω with a 'naive' Legendre structure. It plays the universal role for the data
- J, a (Z/3Z)_S-torsor (the three nonzero 2-torsion points with a cyclic ordering);
- t ∈ Γ(Σ_J^*/S);
- ω ∈ Γ(S, ω_J), the section attached to the torsor structure on J.

The two points of view agree once a section i of μ_4^* (a square root of −1) is fixed. That is, over S̃_0 = μ_4^* ×S_0 with S_0 = Spec Z[1/2].

Why a cyclic order gives ω: ω_J is (as the next page shows) det V_J. A cyclic order on J yields a canonical generator (e_1−e_2)∧(e_2−e_3) of det V_J. One checks this is invariant under cyclic permutations.

**New paragraph: explicit description over an algebraically closed field k.** The curve E is encoded as follows.
- (58) J = ₂E(k)^*, the three nonzero 2-torsion points.
- (59) The 2-dimensional space V_J = Ker(k^J → k) (sum map). Its projective line Σ_J = P^1(V_J) carries the three points ε_i = k·(e_j − e_k) for (i,j,k) a cyclic ordering. Set Σ_J^* = Σ_J − {ε_i}.
- A point t ∈ Σ_J^*, i.e. a line F_t ⊂ V_J.
- (60) A 1-dimensional k-space t = t_E (the Lie algebra / tangent space at the origin).
- (61) An isomorphism ν: t^{⊗2} ≅ T_{Σ_J,t}.

Geometric meaning: Σ_J is the quotient E/{±1} ≅ P^1, the ε_i are the images of the nonzero 2-torsion points, and t is the image of the origin. Since E → Σ is ramified at the origin, the second-order map identifies T_{E,0}^{⊗2} with T_{Σ,t}. This is canonical once 2 is invertible.

So an elliptic curve with this level-2 type structure is the same as a point of P^1 minus three points plus a 'square root' of the tangent line there. This is a coordinate-free form of the classical fact that the λ-line carries the Legendre family as a μ_2-gerbe (the automorphism −1). The page ends announcing the computation of T_{Σ_J,t}. The next page computes it as Hom(F_t, V_J/F_t), with V_J/F_t ≅ F_t^∨ ⊗ det V_J and ω_J = det V_J. It then expresses a Legendre épinglage as κ: t ≅ O_t(1), depending on i ∈ μ_4^*, compatible with ν up to ω.

Purpose: an intrinsic, base-free reconstruction of the Legendre normal form y² = x(x−1)(x−λ) and its canonical differential. This feeds a description of the moduli stack of elliptic curves over Z[1/2] via level-2 data.
errors: No mathematical errors visible. Minor point: the identification t^{⊗2} ≅ T_{Σ,t} via the ramified quotient map is canonical only up to the factor 2 inherent in second derivatives. This is harmless since 2 is invertible (S_0 = Spec Z[1/2]).
The machine transcription duplicates a line ('longue de base' / 'korps de base'); this is a transcription artefact, not an error of Grothendieck.

ideas.what: Description of an elliptic curve (char ≠ 2) by the data (J = nonzero 2-torsion, V_J = Ker(k^J→k), Σ_J = P^1(V_J) with three marked points ε_i, a point t ∈ Σ_J^*, a line t_E with ν: t_E^{⊗2} ≅ T_{Σ_J,t}), i.e. E ↦ E/±1 with branch data
ideas.modern_name: Legendre/λ-line description of M(2) as a μ_2-gerbe over P^1 − {3 points}; elliptic curve as double cover of P^1 branched at 4 points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Legendre, Jacobi); modern moduli form in Igusa, Deligne–Rapoport (1973), Katz–Mazur (1985)

ideas.what: Canonical trivialisation of det V_J (= ω_J) from a cyclic order (Z/3-torsor structure) on J, invariant under cyclic permutations
ideas.modern_name: orientation / determinant line of the reduced permutation representation; A_3-reduction trivialising the sign character

ideas.what: Intrinsic 'Legendre épinglage' (épi-structure) as a rigidification of t_E against O_t(1) ≅ F_t^∨(ω), depending on a choice of i ∈ μ_4^*; universality of a canonical curve E_ω (resp. E_α) for such data
ideas.modern_name: rigidified Legendre family; Legendre structure as a trivialisation of the Lie algebra compatible with the normal-form differential dx/y
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Katz–Mazur and Katz's work on the Legendre family; unsure of an explicit intrinsic treatment

missed.claim: A fully coordinate-free reformulation of the Legendre normal form. The λ-parameter becomes a line F_t in the 3-point-reduced representation V_J, and the Legendre differential becomes an isomorphism t_E ≅ F_t^∨ ⊗ det V_J depending on √−1. This yields a μ_2-torsor of Legendre structures with a universal object over Z[1/2] (resp. Z[1/2, i]). This is a tidy intrinsic packaging, but the underlying mathematics (M(2) as the λ-line gerbe, the Legendre family) is standard.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of modest interest for explicit, choice-free models of level-2 moduli stacks over Z[1/2] and of the role of μ_4 (√−1) in the Legendre form. Likely known in substance to specialists.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful intrinsic set-up of the Legendre family and level-2 data. Conceptually neat and characteristic of Grothendieck, but its content matches classical and Katz–Mazur-era knowledge. Nothing substantively new appears on this page itself.
transcription_corrections: 'S_0 = Spec Z[1/k]' should read 'S_0 = Spec Z[1/2]' (characteristic ≠ 2 setting).

The duplicated lines 'longue de base alg. clos k' / 'korps de base alg. clos k pour simplifier, on se donne' should be a single phrase, roughly: 'du point de vue calculatoire, sur un corps de base alg. clos k pour simplifier, en décrivant la courbe elliptique E sur k en termes des J ...'.
'J (= ₂E(k^s)^*)' is probably 'J (= ₂E(k)^*)', the set of nonzero 2-torsion points (ens. à trois éléments).
Marginal note: 'ε_i = k.(e_j − e_k) si (i,j,k) [cyclique/ordonné], on cons. Σ_J^* = Σ_J − {ε_i}_{i∈J}'.
'Explicitons entièrement la notion d'épinglage [?] des Legendre, des points de vue' should read 'la notion d'épi-structure/épinglage de Legendre, du point de vue calculatoire'.
In (60)–(61), 'k-module inv.' means invertible k-module (a 1-dimensional vector space) t = t_E.
